catalog.title: Reid et al. VLBI high-mass star-forming-region tracers
catalog.credit: Reid et al. (2019); VizieR catalogue J/ApJ/885/131; CDS, Strasbourg
catalog.licenceSummary: VizieR permits scientific use with explicit citation; commercial use depends on the originating journal and is not granted by this receipt.

selection.predicate: All 199 published table rows with positive trigonometric parallax and quoted uncertainty; no additional scientific filtering.
selection.populationBoundary: VLBI masers associated with high-mass star-forming regions; this is neither a complete star census nor an unbiased Galactic-density sample.
selection.armAssignmentBoundary: Published arm designators are retained. Fitted Table 2 segments use subsets and priors, so catalogue-source counts can differ from fit N.

transform.galactocentricConvention: +X from Galactic centre toward the Sun, +Y toward Galactic longitude 90 degrees, +Z toward Galactic north
transform.displayMapping: world x = -heliocentric X, world y = heliocentric Z, world z = heliocentric Y, scaled linearly in scene units per kpc

uncertainty.sourceMeasurements: Per-source parallax, proper-motion, and LSR-velocity 1-sigma uncertainties from the catalogue.
uncertainty.distanceVisualization: Nominal reciprocal parallax d=1/parallax with the reciprocal of parallax plus/minus one quoted sigma stored as a diagnostic span.
uncertainty.distanceCaveat: The reciprocal span is not a Bayesian distance posterior and becomes unbounded when parallax minus one sigma is non-positive.
uncertainty.armModel: Central values and quoted marginal 1-sigma uncertainties transcribed from Table 2. No covariance matrix is published, so the renderer does not combine them into a false joint confidence region.

source.article: Reid et al. (2019), Trigonometric Parallaxes of High-mass Star-forming Regions: Our View of the Milky Way
source.transcriptionNote: Central values and quoted marginal 1-sigma uncertainties transcribed from Table 2. No covariance matrix is published, so the renderer does not combine them into a false joint confidence region.

armModel.azimuthConvention: beta is Galactocentric azimuth; beta=0 lies on the Galactic-centre to Sun line
